table.title: Chronological Table

rows: The Chief of the Nuchen tribe, later Taitsung (太宗) of Ching, gives the name of Taching to his territory, and calls North China, Manchuria.
Russian exploring party reaches the upper stream of the Amur.
Accession of the Emperor Kanghsi (康熙) at Peking.
Russia sends her first envoy to Peking.
The Treaty of Nertchinsk.
The Emperor Kanghsi inspects Outer Mongolia.
Russian envoy arrives: they come frequently in later years.
Kamchatka becomes Russian territory.
Trading at Kulun (庫倫) is first allowed to Russians.
Accession of the Emperor Yungcheng (雍正).
Accession of the Emperor Chienlung (乾隆).
Immigration of the Hans into Manchuria prohibited.
Russia demands the right of navigating the Amur River, but is refused.
Russians come to Kiakhta (恰克圖) for trading.
Accession of the Emperor Chiayang (嘉陽).
Accession of the Emperor Taokuang (道光).
Count Muraviev appointed Governor-General of Eastern Siberia.
Accession of the Emperor Hsienfeng (咸豊).
Count Muraviev descends the Amur River with one thousand soldiers, without obtaining the permission of China.
The Treaty of Aigun.
The Treaty of Peking.
Accession of the Emperor Tungchih (同治).
Accession of the Emperor Kuanghsu (光緒).
Construction of the Siberian Railway begins.
Outbreak of the Sino-Japanese War.
The Treaty of Shimonoseki. Restoration of Liaotung Peninsula to China.
Establishment of Russo-Chinese Bank.
Russo-Chinese Treaty concerning the right of constructing the Chinese Eastern Railway.
Treaty governing the lease of Liaotung Peninsula and the construction of the southern branch of the Chinese Eastern Railway.
The Boxer Rising.
Opening of the Chinese Eastern Railway.
Outbreak of the Russo-Japanese War.
The Treaty of Portsmouth.
E. H. Harriman's proposal to purchase the South Manchuria Railway refused.
South Manchuria Railway Company organized.
First Russo-Japanese Agreement.
Unification of the military administration of the Three Eastern Provinces. Appointment of Hsu Shih-chang as Viceroy of Three Eastern Provinces, and of Tang Shao-yi as Civil Administrator.
The Root-Takahira Agreement.
Accession of the Emperor Hsuantung (宣統).
American financiers obtain the right to construct the Chinchow-Aigun Railway.
Sino-Japanese Agreement concerning the five problems of Manchuria.
Sino-Japanese Agreement regarding Chientao.
American proposal to internationalize the Manchurian railways.
Amalagamation of Korea and Japan.
Second Russo-Japanese Agreement.
Preliminary Currency Reform and Manchurian Commercial Loan Agreement between China and American financiers.
Outbreak of the Revolution.
Chang Tso-lin secures the military power in Fengtien Province.
Declaration of independence by Outer Mongolia.
Establishment of the Republic of China.
Sino-Japanese Treaty respecting the five railways of Manchuria and Mongolia.
Sino-Japanese Treaty respecting South Manchuria and Eastern Inner Mongolia.
Russo-Chinese Treaty.
Chang Tso-lin becomes Military and Civil Governor of Fengtien Province.
The Lansing-Ishii Agreement.
Exchange of notes between Japan and China concerning four railways of Manchuria and Mongolia.
Chang Tso-lin becomes Inspector-General of the Three Eastern Provinces.
Abrogation of the self-government of Outer Mongolia.
The Washington Conference.
First Mukden-Chihli War.
Declaration of independence of the Three Eastern Provinces.
Japan and the United States, recognize the cancellation of the Lansing-Ishii Agreement.
Formation of the Republic of Outer Mongolia.
Second Mukden-Chihli War.
Soviet-Chinese Agreement.
Soviet-Mukden Agreement.
Third Mukden-Chihli War.
Revolt of Kuo Sung-ling.
Chang Tso-lin occupies Peking.
Chang Tso-lin becomes Grand Marshal or Generalissimo.
Chang Tso-lin retreats from Peking; meets an unnatural death. Chang Hsueh-liang succeeds his father.
Revolt of Hulunbuir (Barga) fails.
Three Eastern Provinces hoist the National flag.
Fengtien Province given a new name, Liaoning.
Pressure on Soviet Consulate at Harbin.
Chinese authorities arrest Russian officials of the Chinese Eastern Railway.
Habarovsk Agreement regarding the Chinese Eastern Railway.
Chang Hsueh-liang appointed Deputy-Commander-in-Chief of the National Forces by the Nanking Government.
Formal Soviet-Chinese Conference opened.

table.context: A chronological list of key events in Manchurian and Russian relations from 1636 to 1722, placed under section 3 to give historical background.
transcriber_notes: Transcribed by Claude Haiku 5.5 (via API) from page crops, one reading; not checked by eye.
Rows: 79 (10 on p. 21; the rest from pp. 22-24, which were read separately by Claude Haiku 5.5 (via API) and joined).
